paraphrase: Liberation is free of all saṃsāra, unperturbed, settled, motionless, even and beyond the pairs, mindless and free of thought. Dharma rests on the mind (citta), and the supportless (nirāśraya) gives liberation; god, goddess and all else are beyond dharma and adharma; what rests on dharma and adharma is the bondage of saṃsāra — support is bondage, liberation is supportless.

paraphrase: When the mind is agitated, attached to sense-objects, beings deluded by the impurity of Māyā wander in saṃsāra: this is the settled account of saṃsāra as the pairs.

original.text: सर्वद्वन्द्वविनिर्मुक्तं निश्चितन्तु निराकुलम् । साकुलत्वं यदा चित्तं विषयासक्तचेतसाम् तदा भ्रमन्ति संसारं मायामलविमोहिताः । एतद्द्वन्द्वसमाख्यातं संसारस्य तु निर्णयम्

paraphrase: As long as there is restlessness the mind is unsteady; the unsteady is called 'being' (bhāva), the steady is the mark of liberation; when the mind is joined to thought it is restless, when mind goes beyond mind it is certain and steady; freed from all thought it is still in non-being.

original.text: यथैव सदात्युक्ताः तावच्चित्तं सुचञ्चलम् । चञ्चलं भावमित्युक्तमचलं मुक्तिलक्षणम् चित्तायुक्तं यदा चित्तं तदासौ चञ्चलं स्मृतम् । चित्तातीतं यदा चित्तं निश्चितमचलं भवेत् सर्वचिन्ताविनिर्मुक्तमभावे निश्चलं भवेत् । न योगाध्यातचित्तस्तु न च लक्षणसाधकम्

paraphrase: Consciousness and non-consciousness, imagining and cultivation, concentrations on the circles of sun, moon and fire, air and space, Brahmā, Rudra and the gods — all are called conceptions (kalpanā); those joined to conceptual knowledge wander like a water-wheel and fall quickly into saṃsāra; those in the highest state do not come here.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Jñānakārikā, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00024); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.

paraphrase: Dharma and adharma are the two nooses; cutting the double bond with the sword of knowledge, whither would yogīs go? Bound by that noose they rise and fall and enjoy the store of karma — heaven by dharma, hell and the rest by adharma; the pair dharma-adharma binds the three worlds, and when both are abandoned men are quickly released.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Jñānakārikā, ed. P. C. Bagchi (1934); Muktabodha e-text M00024); paraphrase by U21-natha-aghora from reading the passage.

paraphrase: Mind is of three kinds — tāmasa, restless and petty; rājasa, coming and going; sāttvika, joined to dharma and steady — and there is a fourth mind, free of the three guṇas, always marked by nirvāṇa, the best of all, beyond the senses and imperishable.
